visuals: The golden sand dunes of the Sahara Desert in Algeria under a hot sun. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: While most of the country is the golden Sahara, the north is a lush paradise with the Atlas Mountains and beautiful Mediterranean beaches. It's like two worlds in one!

visuals: The lush green Atlas Mountains in Northern Algeria overlooking the blue Mediterranean coast. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: While most of the country is the golden Sahara, the north is a lush paradise with the Atlas Mountains and beautiful Mediterranean beaches. It's like two worlds in one!

visuals: A vast Algerian Sahara landscape with towering sand dunes, rocky plateaus, and a green oasis with palm trees and camels. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: The Sahara isn't just sand… it’s a mega-landscape! There are towering dunes, rocky plateaus, and secret oases where palm trees grow and camels sip water like it's tea time!

visuals: The Botanical Garden Hamma in Algeria bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And speaking of cool symbols, Algeria’s national animal is the fennec fox. It's tiny, fluffy, and Its giant ears help it stay cool in the desert heat and hear tiny animals moving under the sand.

visuals: A Barbary macaque monkey on the rocky, green slopes of the Atlas Mountains in Algeria. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: You might also bump into a Barbary macaque leaping around the mountains.

visuals: A rare Saharan cheetah with pale spots camouflaged against the sandy landscape of the Algerian desert. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And if you venture waaaaay out into the desert, there's something nearly invisible… the Saharan cheetah. These cats are extremely rare, so spotting one is like finding a hidden treasure.

visuals: The Algiers skyline with its shimmering white historic buildings descending toward the blue Mediterranean Sea. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Now, here’s a quiz for you: What’s the capital of Algeria? Drumroll… it’s Algiers! Often called "Algiers the White" because of its shimmering white buildings reflecting the Mediterranean sun.

visuals: A lively music scene in Oran, Algeria, with people dancing to traditional Rai music. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: There’s more! Oran is a music hotspot, famous for a style called Rai that gets everyone dancing.

visuals: The city of Constantine, Algeria, built around deep ravines with massive stone bridges connecting the cliffs. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And Constantine? It’s wild! The city is built around giant stone bridges hanging over cliffs!

visuals: The Casbah of Algiers in Algeria bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Algerians speak Arabic and Tamazight, and many also speak French. Try saying “Shukran” to say thank you!

visuals: The Tassili n'Ajjer landscape in Algeria bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: As of recent counts, about 45 million people live in Algeria… that’s about as many as all the people in California! Imagine the size of THAT group hug!

visuals: A soccer ball on a soccer field. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Now for my favorite part… food! Couscous is king here! steamed semolina with meat, veggies, and delicious spices, especially on holidays. Yum!

visuals: A traditional Algerian metal teapot pouring hot mint tea into glass cups on a decorated tray. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And guess what you’ll sip while waiting for lunch? Mint tea! It's hot, sweet, and perfect for hanging out with friends or family.

visuals: Bowls of fresh Algerian dates and olives served outdoors under the shade of palm trees in an oasis. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: In the oases, you’ll find plump dates and juicy olives. Some people even make date pastries that taste like sunshine… sticky, sweet, and oh-so-yummy.

visuals: The Maqam Echahid monument in Algeria bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: The Tassili n'Ajjer National Park is like a giant open-air museum, with over 15,000 ancient rock drawings that show how people lived in the Sahara thousands of years ago!

visuals: An Algerian Independence Day parade in Algiers with people in traditional cultural clothing and waving the national flag. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Algeria became independent on July 5th, 1962. It’s the most important day in their history, celebrated with huge parades!

visuals: A soccer ball on a soccer field. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Soccer rules here! The national team, “The Desert Foxes”, won the Africa Cup of Nations in 2019!
